messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate in us-east-1 (5m avg 12% -> 42%). Auto-escalation triggered, on-call: @oncall-alex. :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: ACK. I'm jumping on bridge now. Initial symptoms?

maya-engineering: seeing a lot of model-runner segfaults and timeouts. stacktrace points to attention_kv cache growth then SIGSEGV.

sean-sre: confirming logs from runner-3 and runner-7: repeated doublefree/invalid pointer right after kvcache resize.

erin-support: CS report: a few customers reported timeouts -> 502s and degraded throughput for batch jobs. No data loss reported.

oncall-alex: plan: 1) divert prod traffic off the affected runner group (us-east-infer-1) to fallback pool, 2) disable kv_cache prefix caching for the model family as temporary mitigation, 3) collect core dumps + metrics. I'll start 1 and 2 now.

maya-engineering: +1, disabling kv_cache via feature-flag: 
```json
{ "models": ["rwd-llama-13b"], "kv_cache": "off-temp-325" }
```
Applying to rollout-82.

ops-bot: route-update: /v1/generate traffic 75% -> fallback-pool-us-east completed.

oncall-alex: ops-bot confirms. Throughput dropped but 5xx rate down to ~18% (5m avg). Good sign.

sean-sre: launching cores collection on runner nodes (ssh + gcore). Also capturing `ulimit -c` and kernel dmesg. Command I ran: `sudo systemctl stop inference-runner && sudo gcore -o /var/crash/runner-core $(pgrep runner)`

maya-engineering: grabbing mini reproducer. My hunch: kvcache growth + certain attention kernel path + 4-bit quant path leads to a use-after-free on mm_alloc. Trying to reproduce in canary.

priya-security: any indications of malicious requests? Large prefixes? Unknown. Logs show some long-context requests but no obvious pattern. Tagging for follow-up.

erin-support: flagged top-10 tenants seeing impact and notified account owners. Sending draft status page.

oncall-alex: temporary mitigation summary posted to #status. We should keep fallback routing and kv_cache off for 30 minutes while we validate.

maya-engineering: test canary run failed with segfault at 0x7fff in quant_attention.c: line 214. Minimal repro attached. Will push a hotfix branch that adds bounds checks around kvcache resize.

sean-sre: while hotfix lands, increasing fallback pool capacity by +40% and enabling autoscaler override to avoid coldstarts. `servicectl scale fallback-pool-us-east 14`

ops-bot: scale event succeeded. New pool capacity 14.

oncall-alex: customer-impact update: roughly 6% of requests still hit degraded latency due to routing lag. Support, please keep customers updated.

erin-support: on it. Updating tickets.

maya-engineering: pushed hotfix branch `fix/kv-resize-safety-325` and running CI. If green, will promote to hotpatch to the affected nodes only.

priya-security: please include the core dumps to secure storage S3://redwood-secure/incident-3250012345 and mark as restricted.

sean-sre: cores uploaded and ACLed. Link: https://s3.redwood.internal/secure/incident-3250012345 (restricted).

oncall-alex: CI green, preparing hotpatch. We'll do staged deploy to runner-3 then runner-7. rollback plan in place.

maya-engineering: hotpatch applied to runner-3, monitoring.

ops-bot: runner-3 patched -> health OK. 5xx down to 6% from 42% in peak.

sean-sre: runner-7 patched -> health OK. All patched nodes reporting stable.

oncall-alex: disabling temporary routing now, shifting traffic back to primary pool in 2 waves.

ops-bot: traffic shift complete. Global 5m 5xx now at 1.8%. Latency returned to baseline.

erin-support: customer comms sent: summarized mitigations + ETA for postmortem.

maya-engineering: root cause preliminary: race in kvcache resize path under high concurrent prefix growth -> use-after-free in quant attention kernel. Patch adds atomic resize + defensive null checks. Will open PR for full review.

priya-security: no evidence of data exfil or attack. Marking incident as security-low.

oncall-alex: closing bridge in 15m unless we see regression. Action items: - engr: PR + backport to stable, tests for high-prefix workload; - sres: add kvcache growth alarm and safer defaults; - support: postmortem draft + customer timeline.

sean-sre: will add runbook step to temporarily disable kv_cache on surge and script safe core collection.

erin-support: collecting impacted account list for compensation review.

oncall-alex: thanks everyone. Adding notes to incident tracker. Will ping when postmortem is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
